description: Saldo Pocket is a budget app for iOS and Android. Your budget is stored on your phone: there is no bank connection, and we do not have a copy of your data.

privacy.intro: This policy explains what Saldo Pocket stores, what it sends and to whom, how long it is kept, and what you can do about it. The short version: your budget stays on your phone.

sections.heading: Who is responsible
body: {{company}} (org. no. {{orgNumber}}, {{address}}) is the controller for the processing described here. Contact us at {{email}}.

sections.heading: In short
list: Your budget is stored on your phone. Without an account, we cannot see it.
An account is optional (Apple, Google, Facebook or e-mail). With an account and Pro, your budget is synced to our server in the EU (Ireland), so you can use it on several devices.
There is no bank connection.
CSV and Excel files from your bank are read only on your phone. The file itself is never stored, copied or sent anywhere.

The app sends your budget to our server only when you sync with Pro, and pictures for AI reading only when you have said yes. If backup is turned on on your phone, Apple (iCloud) or Google (your Google account) includes the app's data in it.
Crash reports contain no name, e-mail, account or IP address.
You can export everything and delete everything in the app, for free.

sections.heading: Stored on your phone
body: The app keeps the following in its own storage on your phone. It is not sent to us, and it is deleted when you delete all data in the app or uninstall it:
list: The accounts you create (names you choose, balance and currency; not bank accounts).
Your entries: date, amount, currency, category, vendor and an optional note.
Recurring items, savings goals, your own categories and the category the app remembers for each vendor.
Settings: payday, monthly budget, language and currency, and whether you allow AI reading.
A random device ID. It only leaves the phone as a one-way code, for counting AI readings (see below).
When you are signed in: your sign-in, in the phone's secure storage (the Keychain on iPhone, Android Keystore). It is never included in a backup.
Pictures you choose to keep after an import.
after: KID numbers are never stored, and neither is the full account number. The app may store the last four digits of the account number to recognise the account.

sections.heading: Backup on your phone
body: If backup is turned on, the phone includes the app's data in it: on Android in the backup on your Google account, on iPhone in iCloud. Your budget then comes back on a new phone. Apple and Google store the backup under their own terms, and you turn it on and off in the phone's settings.
Your sign-in and the secure storage are never included, so on a new phone you sign in again.

sections.heading: Importing CSV and Excel files
body: When you import a CSV or Excel file from your bank, the file is read only on your phone. The file itself is never stored, copied or sent anywhere – neither to a server nor to AI.

From the file, only the date (and booking date when the file has it), description, amount, vendor, the bank's balance to reconcile the account, and the last four digits of the account number, to recognise the account, are stored. KID numbers, other references and the file's other columns are not stored.

Entries that are not yet booked are stored as ordinary entries and count straight away. If such an entry is missing from a later import from your bank, the app asks whether you want to remove it. It is never removed by itself.
The app remembers how the file's columns are laid out, without their content, so the next import is quicker. When you are signed in with Pro, this is synced with your other settings.
AI reading is used only for pictures and PDFs, and only when you have said yes.

sections.heading: AI reading of account lists, receipts and invoices (optional)
body: When you import a screenshot or photo of an account list, or scan a receipt or invoice, you can let AI read it. The app asks for permission first, and you can turn it off at any time on the import screen. Without permission, everything is read on your phone and nothing is sent.

With permission, the picture, today's date, the currency, your country, the app's categories (as codes) and the account's column headings (only the headings, not their content) are sent through {{server}} to Anthropic (USA), which reads the entries with its AI model (Claude) and sends them back. The request goes through the Supabase server closest to you; neither we nor Supabase store the picture or the entries. Anthropic does not use data sent through its API to train its models, and deletes it within {{anthropicDays}} days ({{linkAnthropic}}).

To keep the service within its limits, our server counts AI readings per device and day. The phone sends only a one-way code made from the random device ID, and the server makes a new code from it with a secret key before it is stored, so the count cannot be linked to you or your account. Only the code, the date and the number are stored, and the count is deleted automatically after {{aiCountDays}} days.

Only in the free version: for the limit on AI scans, the phone sends a one-way code made from the phone's ID, never the ID itself. The server makes a new code from it with a secret key and stores only that, the month, whether it is a test version, and the number. The hashed device ID is used only to count free AI scans, not for tracking, and the count is deleted automatically after {{scanCountMonths}} months. With Pro, no phone ID is sent.

sections.heading: Scanning receipts and invoices
body: When you scan a receipt or invoice, the picture is read on your phone, or by AI if you have said yes (see above). The picture is deleted as soon as it has been read, even if you cancel or something goes wrong. From the picture, only the store, date, amount and category are stored. KID and account numbers are never stored.

sections.heading: Crash reports
body: When the app crashes or an error occurs, a report is sent to Sentry (EU, Germany): what went wrong and where in the app, what happened just before (without content from your budget), the app version, and the phone model and system version. Sentry does not store the IP address, and the reports contain no name, e-mail or account. They are kept for at most {{crashMaxDays}} days and are used only to fix errors.

sections.heading: App updates
body: Each time it starts, the app asks Expo (USA), the service that delivers updates, whether there is a new one. Expo then receives the IP address, the platform (iOS or Android), the app's version and a random ID for the installation – nothing about you or your budget.

sections.heading: Buying Pro
body: Pro is bought in the App Store or Google Play. Apple or Google handle the payment under their own privacy policies; we never see your card details.

RevenueCat (USA) keeps track of whether you have Pro. The app contacts RevenueCat each time it starts, also in the free version, with an anonymous customer ID that RevenueCat creates, or your account ID when you are signed in, so Pro follows your account. RevenueCat receives the purchases and receipts from the store, the platform and the app's version. In test versions and for test purchases, the customer is marked as a test. The purchase history stays with the store and RevenueCat even if you delete your account, so your purchase is not lost.

sections.heading: Optional account and sync (Pro)
body: You can sign in with Apple, Google, Facebook (Meta) or e-mail. Sign-in is handled by Supabase on servers in {{region}}. We then store your e-mail address, an account ID, your name if the provider shares it, your app language and, in test versions, a test flag. With Apple you can hide your e-mail address; we then see only Apple's relay address.

With Pro, your budget is synced to your account: accounts, entries, recurring items, budget, savings goals, your own categories, vendors the app remembers and the settings that follow you (payday, salary, budget). Each change is stored with when it was made and on which device. The data is encrypted in transit and at rest, and only your account can read it.

Sign-in codes and links are sent by e-mail through Resend (USA), with your address and language. The link opens our website, hosted by Vercel, which passes you on to the app. To send each e-mail only once, our server keeps only the message ID, type and status for {{emailLogDays}} days, never the address.

You can sign out at any time; your data stays on the phone. «Delete account» removes the account and all data stored with it on our server. What stays: the purchase history with the store and RevenueCat, the counts with no name or account (deleted after {{aiCountDays}} days and {{scanCountMonths}} months) and the services' own logs under their terms.

sections.heading: Widget and reminders
body: The widget shows figures from the data on your phone, and reminders about recurring items are set up on your phone. Nothing is sent for either.

sections.heading: Who we share data with
list: Supabase (Ireland, EU): sign-in, sync for Pro, the server for AI reading and the counts.
Anthropic (USA): AI reading, only with your permission.
Resend (USA): e-mails with sign-in codes and links.
RevenueCat (USA): Pro status and purchases.
Sentry (EU, Germany): crash reports, without IP address.
Expo (USA): app updates.
Vercel (USA): our website, including the page the sign-in link opens.
Apple, Google and Meta: the App Store, Google Play, signing in with them when you choose to, and the phone's backup.
Exchange rates: our server fetches rates from Frankfurter and ExchangeRate-API. No data about you is sent there.
after: Where data goes to the USA, the providers use the EU standard contractual clauses or the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. We never sell data, and the app has no ads and no tracking.

sections.heading: Legal basis
list: To provide the app you use (GDPR Article 6(1)(b)): account and sync (Supabase), signing in with Apple, Google, Facebook or e-mail (Resend), and buying Pro (App Store, Google Play and RevenueCat).
Your consent to AI reading (Article 6(1)(a)), through Supabase to Anthropic. You can withdraw it at any time.
Our legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f)) in fixing errors (Sentry), delivering app updates (Expo), keeping the service within its limits (the counts) and running the website (Vercel).

sections.heading: How long data is kept
list: On your phone: until you delete it in the app or uninstall the app.
Your account and synced data: until you delete your account in the app.
Pictures for AI reading: not stored by us. At Anthropic: deleted within {{anthropicDays}} days, except requests flagged for misuse ({{linkAnthropic}}).
CSV and Excel files you import: not stored. Only the entries you save and the layout of the file's columns remain.
Count of AI readings (one-way code, date and number): {{aiCountDays}} days.
Count of free AI scans (hashed device ID, month and number): {{scanCountMonths}} months.
Log of sign-in e-mails (without the address): {{emailLogDays}} days.
Crash reports: at most {{crashMaxDays}} days.

Sign-in e-mails at Resend: {{resendDays}} days ({{linkResend}}). Supabase's own logs and backups: at most {{supabaseLogDays}} days ({{linkSupabase}}). RevenueCat ({{linkRevenueCat}}), Expo ({{linkExpo}}) and Vercel ({{linkVercel}}): under their terms, which give no fixed period.
Backup on your phone: with Apple or Google, under their terms, until you delete it.

sections.heading: Your rights
body: You can see, correct and export all your data in the app ({{menuMe}} → {{menuExport}}, free for everyone), and delete it ({{menuMe}} → {{menuDelete}}). You can object to the processing and withdraw your consent to AI reading at any time.

If you have questions, write to {{email}}. The supervisory authority is the Norwegian Data Protection Authority (Datatilsynet), and you can complain to it. If you live in the EU/EEA, you can also complain to the data protection authority in your own country.

sections.heading: Children
body: Saldo Pocket is not made for children under 13, and we do not knowingly process their data.

sections.heading: Changes
body: If we change this policy, we update this page and the date at the top. If the change matters for how your data is used, we let you know in the app.

deleteAccount.intro: Your Saldo Pocket data is stored on your phone, so you delete it yourself in the app. No request is needed.

sections.heading: Delete everything in the app
body: This deletes everything the app has on your phone: accounts, entries, recurring items, goals, categories, vendors, settings, your sign-in, saved pictures and files, the widget's data, the device ID and your choice of language and currency. The app then starts again as new.
The count of free scans and file imports stays – only numbers, nothing about you or your data – both on the phone and on our server, so the free limit still applies.
It cannot be undone. If you want a copy, export your data first under {{menuMe}} → {{menuExport}}. It is free.

sections.heading: Uninstalling the app
body: Uninstalling Saldo Pocket also deletes all its data from your phone.

Exception: the count of free scans and file imports (only numbers) may stay in the phone's keychain (iPhone) or in Android's backup, so the free limit still applies after a new installation. If backup is turned on on your phone, a copy of the app's data stays with Apple or Google until you delete it there.

sections.heading: What is left on our server
body: If you have used AI reading, our server has a count of readings per device and day, stored as a one-way code and without any content. It is deleted automatically after {{aiCountDays}} days and cannot be linked to you.

Free AI scans are also counted per month with a hashed device ID (a one-way code, never the ID itself). The hashed device ID is used only to count free AI scans, not for tracking, and the count is deleted automatically after {{scanCountMonths}} months.
Your purchase and purchase history stay with the App Store or Google Play and RevenueCat, so you can restore Pro. The services we use have their own logs, which are deleted under their terms.

sections.heading: Deleting your account
body: If you use the app without signing in, your data is only on your phone. It is deleted when you delete all data in the app, or when you remove the app from your phone.

If you are signed in, the data in the cloud is also deleted when you delete your account in the app: the account, everything synced to it, and everything on the phone you delete from. If you signed in with Facebook, what we got from Facebook is deleted too. You can also remove Saldo Pocket in your Facebook settings. What stays is described above.

If you only delete the data on your phone, you are signed out, but your account and your data in the cloud stay. Data on your other devices is not deleted automatically; delete it in the app there. Deleting does not cancel a subscription; you do that in the App Store or Google Play.

sections.heading: If you no longer have the app
body: Write to {{email}} with the subject «Delete Saldo Pocket data». We reply within 30 days. If you used the app without signing in, we usually have nothing stored about you, and we confirm that. If you had an account, give the e-mail address you signed in with, and we delete the account and the data in the cloud and confirm it.

support.intro: Questions, problems or ideas? Write to us and we will answer as soon as we can.
support.contactBody: E-mail {{email}}. Please tell us your phone model and the app version (at the bottom of Me).
support.proNote: See Pro in the app for what is included.

faq.q: How do I restore my purchase on a new phone?
faq.a: Pro is tied to your Apple ID or Google account. Sign in with the same account on the new phone, open Saldo Pocket and tap Restore purchases.

faq.q: How do I export my data?
faq.a: Go to Me → Export data. Export all my data (JSON or CSV) is free for everyone.

faq.q: How do I import from my online bank?
faq.a: Tap + and choose how you want to bring in your transactions (screenshots or a file from your online bank). You review every row before anything is saved, and rows you already have are marked. Saldo Pocket never connects to your bank.

faq.q: How do I delete my data?
faq.a: Go to Me → Delete all data. Everything on the phone is deleted. Read more on the page about deleting your data.

terms.intro: These terms apply when you use Saldo Pocket, a budgeting app from {{company}}. By using the app, you accept them.

sections.heading: Who we are
body: {{company}} (org. no. {{orgNumber}}, {{country}}) makes and runs Saldo Pocket. Contact us at {{email}}.

sections.heading: What the app is
body: Saldo Pocket gives you an overview of your money: accounts, entries, budget and goals. The figures are based on what you enter and import. They are an overview, not financial advice, so check important decisions with your bank.

sections.heading: Account and sync
body: You can use the app without an account. If you sign in and have Pro, your data is synced to your account so you can use it on several devices. Keep your sign-in safe; anyone who can sign in to your account can see the synced data.

sections.heading: Free and Pro
body: The free version costs nothing. Pro is bought in the App Store or Google Play, as a subscription (monthly or yearly) or as a one-time purchase. The price is shown in the store before you buy.
list: A subscription renews automatically until you cancel it in the store at least 24 hours before the period ends.
You manage and cancel it in your App Store or Google Play account settings.
If a free trial is offered, it turns into a paid subscription when it ends unless you cancel before then.

sections.heading: The stores’ terms
body: Purchases on iPhone and iPad also follow Apple’s standard license agreement (EULA), and purchases on Android follow Google Play’s terms. Refunds are handled by the store you bought from.

sections.heading: Your data
body: Your data is yours. You can export it and delete it in the app at any time, even on the free version. How we handle personal data is described in the privacy policy.

sections.heading: Responsibility
body: We work to keep the app correct and available, but it is provided as is. As far as the law allows, we are not responsible for indirect losses. Your rights as a consumer are not limited by these terms.

sections.heading: Changes
body: We may update these terms. Important changes are shown in the app or on this page, with the date at the top.

sections.heading: Law
body: These terms are governed by Norwegian law. If you are a consumer, you also keep the protection given to you by the law of the country where you live.
